hints: Apply the sum-to-product differences $\sin A-\sin B=2\cos\frac{A+B}{2}\sin\frac{A-B}{2}$ and $\cos A-\cos B=-2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\sin\frac{A-B}{2}$.
This turns the equation into $2\cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{6}=-2\sin x\sin\frac{\pi}{3}$.
Insert the exact special-angle values and divide by $\cos x$ to isolate $\tan x$.
walkthrough:
Apply the compound angle formulae to the left-hand side:
$$\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \sin x\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) + \cos x\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x$$
$$\sin\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \sin x\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - \cos x\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x$$
$$\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - \sin\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos x\right) = \cos x$$

Apply the compound angle formulae to the right-hand side:
$$\cos\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos x\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) - \sin x\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x$$
$$\cos\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos x\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) + \sin x\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x$$
$$\cos\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) - \cos\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = -2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x\right) = -\sqrt{3}\sin x$$

Equate the two sides:
$$\cos x = -\sqrt{3}\sin x$$

Divide both sides by $-\sqrt{3}\cos x$ to obtain $\tan x$:
$$\tan x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

hints: Begin with the result from part (a), $\tan x=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$.
Use the reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$ and the fact that tangent is negative in quadrants II and IV.
List both angles in $0\leq x\leq2\pi$ and exclude any values outside this interval.
walkthrough:
Identify the reference angle for $\tan x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$:
$$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$$

Find the roots in the second quadrant for $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 2\pi$:
$$x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6}\pi$$

Find the roots in the fourth quadrant for $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 2\pi$:
$$x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{11}{6}\pi$$

State both exact solutions in the interval $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 2\pi$:
$$x = \dfrac{5}{6}\pi \quad \text{and} \quad x = \dfrac{11}{6}\pi$$
